```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Javidi 2026 is a model-based meta-analysis (MBMA) that uses published
aggregate trial data to project efficacy into an indication a drug has not been
studied in. Its worked example bridges plaque psoriasis (PsO) and psoriatic
arthritis (PsA). It has two steps, and this package ships the three fitted
models as three files:

* `Javidi_2026_psoriaticDisease_bridging_mbma` -- **Model 1**, the
  cross-indication bridge. One nonlinear mixed-effects longitudinal
  dose-response model fitted jointly to PASI75 in PsO, PASI75 in PsA and ACR20
  in PsA (66 trials, 190 arms, 30,450 participants). It exposes the three
  outputs `prob_pasi75` (PsO), `prob_pasi75_psa` and `prob_acr20` (PsA).
* `Javidi_2026_psa_acr50_acr70_wk16_mbma` and
  `Javidi_2026_psa_acr50_acr70_wk24_mbma` -- **Model 2**, the cross-endpoint
  bridge within PsA. The logit of an arm's ACR50 or ACR70 rate is a linear
  function of the same arm's ACR20 rate, with a drug-class slope. The authors
  fitted it separately to week-16 and week-24 data (27 trials, 78 arms,
  11,326 participants), so each week is its own file.

The paper chains the two: Model 1 projects ACR20 for a new indication, and
Model 2 turns that ACR20 into ACR50 and ACR70.

* Article: Javidi M, et al. CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol.
  2026;15(5):726-740. <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70207> (PMC13142780).
* Supporting Information (Data S1): the authors' complete R code (nlme `nlme()`
  for Model 1, `gnls()` for Model 2), Equations S.2.1-S.6 and every parameter
  estimate (Tables S1-S3). No estimate is in the main text.
* No erratum was found (Europe PMC search, 2026-11-13).

```{r models}
mod1 <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Javidi_2026_psoriaticDisease_bridging_mbma"))
mod2wk16 <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Javidi_2026_psa_acr50_acr70_wk16_mbma"))
mod2wk24 <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Javidi_2026_psa_acr50_acr70_wk24_mbma"))
typ1 <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod1)
typ2wk16 <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod2wk16)
typ2wk24 <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod2wk24)
```

# Population

All three models work at the **study-arm** level: one observation is one
trial arm's responder rate at one time, not one patient's outcome. Model 1's
random effects are between-trial, and Model 2 has none.

The data came from a vendor-curated database of randomised, parallel-group,
placebo- or active-controlled PsO and PsA trials published 2000-2023, built
following the Cochrane Handbook and PRISMA (Methods 'Data'). Sixty-seven phase
2 / phase 3 trials of 11 drugs were selected (34 PsO, 33 PsA; Supporting
Information Table S5): adalimumab, apremilast, bimekizumab, deucravacitinib,
etanercept, guselkumab, ixekizumab, risankizumab, secukinumab, tofacitinib and
ustekinumab, plus brepocitinib in Model 2. Model 1 kept only compounds studied
in both indications. Longitudinal data run to 52 weeks; data after a
re-randomisation, a regimen change or substantial drop-out were excluded. The
deucravacitinib PsA phase 2 trial (IM011-084) was held out of both models for
external validation. No arm-level demographics are reported.

# Source trace

Every equation and every `ini()` value, with where it came from. The in-file
comments carry the same trace per line.

```{r source-trace-equations}
tibble::tribble(
  ~Component, ~Source,
  "Y = p + eps, Var(eps) = p (1 - p) / N", "Equations 1 and 1.1; Data S1 Model 1 code (varPower(0.5) on fitted*(1 - fitted)/n, sigma = 1)",
  "p = inverse-logit(pbo + tr.eff)", "Equation 1.2",
  "pbo = p.eff + plsp * (1 - exp(-k.pbo * t)) + eta", "Equation 2; k.pbo enters the code as exp(pk)",
  "p.eff = indication / endpoint intercepts + p.eff.ph3 on phase 3 placebo arms", "Equation S.2.1",
  "tr.eff = drg.eff * (1 - exp(-k.drg * t)), k.drg = k.drg.psa + k.drg.psa.acr20 + k.drug", "Equations 3 and S.3.1; code exp(k)",
  "drg.eff = c.eff + EMAX * dose / (dose + ED50) + X + gamma", "Equation 3.2; code exp(ed50)",
  "c.eff, EMAX, ED50, X shifts by indication / endpoint / phase", "Equations S.3.2.1-S.3.2.4",
  "(eta, gamma) ~ N(0, omega), block-diagonal 6 x 6", "Equation 4; Table S2 (A.)",
  "Model 2: logit(Y_s) = slp * ACR20 + intc_s", "Equation 5; Data S1 Model 2 code",
  "slp = slp.ph3 + slp.acr + slp.drg.class + slp.prtnf * prTNF", "Equation S.6",
  "Model 2 residual: Var(logit) = 1 / (p (1 - p) n), p = ACR20", "Data S1 Model 2 code (varFixed(~mdl.weights), sigma = 1)"
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Structural, covariate and residual equations.")
```

```{r source-trace-params}
tibble::tribble(
  ~Block, ~Parameters, ~Source,
  "Model 1 placebo", "p.eff.pso, p.eff.psa, p.eff.psa.acr20, p.eff.ph3, plsp, k.pbo", "Table S1",
  "Model 1 treatment shifts", "drg.eff.psa, drg.eff.psa.acr20, drg.eff.ph3 (PsO, PsA)", "Table S1",
  "Model 1 dose-independent drugs", "x.psa, x.psa.acr20, x.drg for 7 drugs", "Table S1",
  "Model 1 dose-response drugs", "emax.psa.acr20, ed50.psa, ed50.psa.acr20, emax.drg / ed50.drg for 4 drugs", "Table S1",
  "Model 1 onset", "k.drg.psa, k.drg.psa.acr20, k.drug for 10 drugs (tofacitinib = reference, 0)", "Table S1; Data S1 code formula",
  "Model 1 random effects", "6 variances, 4 covariances", "Table S2 (A.)",
  "Model 1 / 2 residual", "sigma = 1 (fixed)", "Data S1 nlmeControl / gnlsControl(sigma = 1)",
  "Model 2 week 16", "8 class slopes, slp.acr, slp.ph3, slp.prtnf, 2 intercepts", "Table S3, 16wk rows",
  "Model 2 week 24", "7 class slopes, slp.acr, slp.ph3, slp.prtnf, 2 intercepts", "Table S3, 24wk rows",
  "Normalised-dose reference regimens", "guselkumab 100 mg q8w, tofacitinib 5 mg BID, secukinumab 300 mg, deucravacitinib 6 mg QD", "derived from Figure S6 and Table S4 (see below)",
  "Prior-TNF normalisation", "(PRIOR_TNF_PCT - 57) / 19", "centre: Figures S15 / S20 captions; scale: derived from Figure S19"
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Parameter provenance by block.")
```

# Study arms

Model 1 takes treatment through one `TRT_<INN>` indicator per drug; the four
drugs with a dose-response model also take a normalised dose
`DOSE_<DRUG>_REL` (1 = the reference regimen). Phase enters through
`STUDY_PHASE3`, and `N_ARM` is needed only by the residual.

```{r arm-helper}
trtCols <- c(
  "TRT_ADALIMUMAB", "TRT_APREMILAST", "TRT_BIMEKIZUMAB", "TRT_DEUCRAVACITINIB",
  "TRT_ETANERCEPT", "TRT_GUSELKUMAB", "TRT_IXEKIZUMAB", "TRT_RISANKIZUMAB",
  "TRT_SECUKINUMAB", "TRT_TOFACITINIB", "TRT_USTEKINUMAB"
)
doseCols <- c(
  "DOSE_GUSELKUMAB_REL", "DOSE_TOFACITINIB_REL", "DOSE_SECUKINUMAB_REL",
  "DOSE_DEUCRAVACITINIB_REL"
)

#' One Model 1 arm: observations at `times` for `drug` (NA = placebo).
model1Arm <- function(id, drug = NA, relDose = 0, phase3 = 0, times = c(16, 24),
                      nArm = 100) {
  d <- data.frame(id = id, time = times, STUDY_PHASE3 = phase3, N_ARM = nArm)
  for (cc in c(trtCols, doseCols)) d[[cc]] <- 0
  if (!is.na(drug)) {
    d[[paste0("TRT_", drug)]] <- 1
    doseCol <- paste0("DOSE_", drug, "_REL")
    if (doseCol %in% doseCols) d[[doseCol]] <- relDose
  }
  d
}

classCols <- c(
  "TRT_PDE4_INHIBITOR", "TRT_ANTITNF", "TRT_ANTIIL17", "TRT_ANTIIL17AF",
  "TRT_ANTIIL23", "TRT_ANTIIL12_23", "TRT_TYK2_INHIBITOR"
)

#' One Model 2 arm at week `wk` for drug class `cls` (NA = placebo).
model2Arm <- function(id, acr20Pct, cls = NA, phase3 = 0, priorTnfPct = 57,
                      wk = 16, nArm = 100) {
  d <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = wk, RESP_ACR20_PCT = acr20Pct, STUDY_PHASE3 = phase3,
    PRIOR_TNF_PCT = priorTnfPct, N_ARM = nArm
  )
  for (cc in classCols) d[[cc]] <- 0
  if (!is.na(cls)) d[[cls]] <- 1
  d
}
```

# Model 1: cross-indication bridge

## Reproducing Table 1 (Model 1 rows)

Table 1 projects the three Model 1 endpoints at weeks 16 and 24 for placebo
and the anti-TNF class in phase 2 and phase 3 trials. The paper defines the
anti-TNF class as the average treatment effect of adalimumab and etanercept;
both arms share the same placebo part, so the class logit is the mean of the
two drugs' logits.

```{r table1-model1}
armsT1 <- bind_rows(
  model1Arm(1, phase3 = 0), model1Arm(2, phase3 = 1),
  model1Arm(3, "ADALIMUMAB", phase3 = 0), model1Arm(4, "ADALIMUMAB", phase3 = 1),
  model1Arm(5, "ETANERCEPT", phase3 = 0), model1Arm(6, "ETANERCEPT", phase3 = 1)
)
armKey <- tibble(
  id = 1:6, phase = rep(2:3, 3),
  arm = rep(c("Placebo", "Adalimumab", "Etanercept"), each = 2)
)
sol1 <- rxode2::rxSolve(typ1, armsT1, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  select(id, time, prob_pasi75, prob_pasi75_psa, prob_acr20) |>
  left_join(armKey, by = "id") |>
  pivot_longer(starts_with("prob_"), names_to = "output", values_to = "p") |>
  mutate(
    Treatment = ifelse(arm == "Placebo", "Placebo", "Anti-TNF class"),
    logitP = qlogis(p)
  ) |>
  group_by(Treatment, phase, output, time) |>
  summarise(sim = 100 * plogis(mean(logitP)), .groups = "drop")

# Javidi 2026 Table 1, Model 1 rows: projected value [95% CI].
pub1 <- tribble(
  ~Treatment, ~phase, ~output, ~time, ~pub, ~lo, ~hi,
  "Placebo", 2, "prob_pasi75", 16, 8.28, 6.95, 9.85,
  "Placebo", 2, "prob_pasi75", 24, 9.02, 7.59, 10.71,
  "Placebo", 2, "prob_pasi75_psa", 16, 11.07, 9.22, 13.23,
  "Placebo", 2, "prob_pasi75_psa", 24, 11.29, 9.41, 13.49,
  "Placebo", 2, "prob_acr20", 16, 22.47, 19.62, 25.58,
  "Placebo", 2, "prob_acr20", 24, 22.87, 19.99, 26,
  "Placebo", 3, "prob_pasi75", 16, 8.78, 7.66, 10.07,
  "Placebo", 3, "prob_pasi75", 24, 9.57, 8.34, 10.97,
  "Placebo", 3, "prob_pasi75_psa", 16, 11.72, 10.19, 13.44,
  "Placebo", 3, "prob_pasi75_psa", 24, 11.95, 10.39, 13.72,
  "Placebo", 3, "prob_acr20", 16, 23.62, 21.62, 25.73,
  "Placebo", 3, "prob_acr20", 24, 24.03, 21.98, 26.2,
  "Anti-TNF class", 2, "prob_pasi75", 16, 57.89, 51.77, 63.79,
  "Anti-TNF class", 2, "prob_pasi75", 24, 60.76, 54.6, 66.59,
  "Anti-TNF class", 2, "prob_pasi75_psa", 16, 43.97, 36.58, 51.44,
  "Anti-TNF class", 2, "prob_pasi75_psa", 24, 52.14, 43.22, 60.55,
  "Anti-TNF class", 2, "prob_acr20", 16, 47.55, 36.07, 59.13,
  "Anti-TNF class", 2, "prob_acr20", 24, 48.2, 36.62, 59.85,
  "Anti-TNF class", 3, "prob_pasi75", 16, 65.48, 61.8, 69.01,
  "Anti-TNF class", 3, "prob_pasi75", 24, 68.24, 64.58, 71.7,
  "Anti-TNF class", 3, "prob_pasi75_psa", 16, 39.17, 34.87, 43.76,
  "Anti-TNF class", 3, "prob_pasi75_psa", 24, 46.36, 41.47, 51.39,
  "Anti-TNF class", 3, "prob_acr20", 16, 39.8, 31.23, 48.93,
  "Anti-TNF class", 3, "prob_acr20", 24, 40.4, 31.75, 49.6
)
cmp1 <- inner_join(pub1, sol1, by = c("Treatment", "phase", "output", "time")) |>
  mutate(diff = sim - pub)
stopifnot(nrow(cmp1) == nrow(pub1))

cmp1 |>
  transmute(
    Treatment, Phase = phase, Output = output, Week = time,
    `Published [95% CI]` = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", pub, lo, hi),
    `Simulated` = sprintf("%.2f", sim), `Difference` = sprintf("%+.2f", diff)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Model 1 typical values against Javidi 2026 Table 1 (percent responders).")

# Deterministic typical values against the centre of the paper's 50,000-draw
# parameter-uncertainty simulation. Rows driven by well-determined terms agree
# to rounding; rows driven by the slow, uncertain PsA drug onset rate can sit a
# fraction of a point off, because the centre of a nonlinear function of
# uncertain parameters is not the function at their estimates.
stopifnot(
  median(abs(cmp1$diff)) < 0.1,
  max(abs(cmp1$diff)) < 1,
  all(cmp1$sim >= cmp1$lo & cmp1$sim <= cmp1$hi)
)
```

The placebo rows and every PASI75-in-PsO and ACR20 row of Table 1 are
reproduced to within about 0.1 percentage point (median absolute difference
`r sprintf("%.2f", median(abs(cmp1$diff)))`). The anti-TNF PASI75-in-PsA rows
are off by up to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(abs(cmp1$diff)))` points. Those are the
rows governed by the slowest and least certain onset rate (PsA shift
k.drg.psa = -1.72 on the log scale): Table 1 reports the centre of 50,000
parameter-uncertainty draws, and for a strongly nonlinear term that centre
need not equal the typical value. Every row lies inside its published interval.

## External validation: deucravacitinib in PsA (Table S4)

The paper's headline application: deucravacitinib was studied in psoriasis,
and its PsA trial IM011-084 was withheld from fitting. Model 1 projects that
phase 2 trial's ACR20 and PASI75 at week 16 for placebo, 6 mg QD and 12 mg QD.

```{r tableS4-model1}
armsS4 <- bind_rows(
  model1Arm(1, times = 16),
  model1Arm(2, "DEUCRAVACITINIB", relDose = 1, times = 16),
  model1Arm(3, "DEUCRAVACITINIB", relDose = 2, times = 16)
)
solS4 <- rxode2::rxSolve(typ1, armsS4, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(Arm = c("Placebo", "Deucravacitinib 6 mg QD", "Deucravacitinib 12 mg QD")[id])

pubS4 <- tribble(
  ~Arm, ~Endpoint, ~observed, ~pub, ~lo, ~hi,
  "Placebo", "ACR20", 31.8, 22.7, 10.6, 36.4,
  "Placebo", "PASI75", 20.4, 11.1, 3.7, 20.4,
  "Deucravacitinib 6 mg QD", "ACR20", 52.9, 51.4, 14.3, 87.1,
  "Deucravacitinib 6 mg QD", "PASI75", 42.4, 37.3, 20.3, 57.6,
  "Deucravacitinib 12 mg QD", "ACR20", 62.7, 55.2, 14.9, 89.6,
  "Deucravacitinib 12 mg QD", "PASI75", 59.6, 44.2, 25, 65.4
)
simS4 <- solS4 |>
  transmute(Arm, ACR20 = 100 * prob_acr20, PASI75 = 100 * prob_pasi75_psa) |>
  pivot_longer(c(ACR20, PASI75), names_to = "Endpoint", values_to = "sim")
cmpS4 <- inner_join(pubS4, simS4, by = c("Arm", "Endpoint")) |>
  mutate(diff = sim - pub)

cmpS4 |>
  transmute(
    Arm, Endpoint, `Observed (IM011-084)` = observed,
    `Published projection [95% PI]` = sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]", pub, lo, hi),
    Simulated = sprintf("%.1f", sim), Difference = sprintf("%+.1f", diff)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Model 1 week-16 projections for IM011-084 against Javidi 2026 Table S4 (percent responders).")

stopifnot(max(abs(cmpS4$diff)) < 1.5)
```

The 6 mg QD = 1 and 12 mg QD = 2 normalised doses reproduce all four active
projections to within about one percentage point, which is how the
deucravacitinib reference regimen was confirmed.

## Normalised dose of the other dose-response drugs (Figure S6)

The paper normalises dose 'by the approved dose or the most frequent tested
dose for each compound' without listing the reference regimens. Its
Figure S6 draws the Model 1 ACR20 curve for every PsA regimen in a potential
phase 3 trial, and the plateaus pin the reference: guselkumab 100 mg q8w = 1
(q4w = 2), tofacitinib 5 mg BID = 1 (10 mg BID = 2), and secukinumab
300 mg = 1 (150 mg = 0.5, 75 mg = 0.25). The figure below redraws those
curves from the packaged model; compare it with Figure S6.

```{r figS6, fig.cap = "Model 1 ACR20 in PsA, potential phase 3 trial, for the dose-response drugs at the recovered normalised doses. Replicates the guselkumab, secukinumab and tofacitinib panels of Javidi 2026 Supporting Information Figure S6 (plateaus about 0.64 / 0.66, 0.44 / 0.47 / 0.52 and 0.42 / 0.44)."}
regimens <- tribble(
  ~label, ~drug, ~rel,
  "guselkumab 100 mg q8w", "GUSELKUMAB", 1,
  "guselkumab 100 mg q4w", "GUSELKUMAB", 2,
  "secukinumab 75 mg", "SECUKINUMAB", 0.25,
  "secukinumab 150 mg", "SECUKINUMAB", 0.5,
  "secukinumab 300 mg", "SECUKINUMAB", 1,
  "tofacitinib 5 mg BID", "TOFACITINIB", 1,
  "tofacitinib 10 mg BID", "TOFACITINIB", 2
)
armsS6 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  model1Arm(i, regimens$drug[i], regimens$rel[i], phase3 = 1, times = seq(0, 24, by = 0.5))
}))
solS6 <- rxode2::rxSolve(typ1, armsS6, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(regimen = regimens$label[id], drug = tolower(regimens$drug[id]))

ggplot(solS6, aes(time, prob_acr20, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~drug) +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "ACR20 (proportion of patients)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

plateau <- solS6 |> filter(time == 24) |> select(regimen, prob_acr20)
knitr::kable(plateau, digits = 3, caption = "Week-24 ACR20 at the recovered normalised doses.")
```

## Figure 5: endpoints across indications

Figure 5 of the paper simulates the three Model 1 endpoints to week 24 for
placebo and the anti-TNF class, by study phase.

```{r fig5, fig.cap = "Typical PASI75 (PsO), PASI75 (PsA) and ACR20 (PsA) over 24 weeks for placebo and the anti-TNF class (mean logit of adalimumab and etanercept). Replicates the central lines of Javidi 2026 Figure 5; the paper's shaded 95% CIs come from parameter uncertainty, which is not part of the packaged model."}
armsF5 <- bind_rows(
  model1Arm(1, phase3 = 0, times = seq(0, 24, by = 0.5)),
  model1Arm(2, phase3 = 1, times = seq(0, 24, by = 0.5)),
  model1Arm(3, "ADALIMUMAB", phase3 = 0, times = seq(0, 24, by = 0.5)),
  model1Arm(4, "ADALIMUMAB", phase3 = 1, times = seq(0, 24, by = 0.5)),
  model1Arm(5, "ETANERCEPT", phase3 = 0, times = seq(0, 24, by = 0.5)),
  model1Arm(6, "ETANERCEPT", phase3 = 1, times = seq(0, 24, by = 0.5))
)
solF5 <- rxode2::rxSolve(typ1, armsF5, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  select(id, time, prob_pasi75, prob_pasi75_psa, prob_acr20) |>
  left_join(armKey, by = "id") |>
  pivot_longer(starts_with("prob_"), names_to = "output", values_to = "p") |>
  mutate(Treatment = ifelse(arm == "Placebo", "Placebo", "Anti-TNF class")) |>
  group_by(Treatment, phase, output, time) |>
  summarise(p = plogis(mean(qlogis(p))), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    output = factor(output,
      levels = c("prob_pasi75", "prob_pasi75_psa", "prob_acr20"),
      labels = c("PASI75 in PsO", "PASI75 in PsA", "ACR20 in PsA")
    ),
    Phase = paste("Phase", phase)
  )

ggplot(solF5, aes(time, 100 * p, colour = Treatment, linetype = Phase)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~output) +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Responders (%)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

As the paper notes, PASI75 has a much wider dynamic range in PsO than in PsA,
and the phase 3 anti-TNF effect is larger in PsO but smaller in PsA than in
phase 2.

## Between-trial variability

Model 1's random effects describe how much trials differ. The 95% prediction
interval Table S4 reports for the IM011-084 deucravacitinib 6 mg ACR20
projection, 14.3% to 87.1%, is dominated by the large between-trial variance
of the ACR20 treatment effect (0.628 on the logit scale). Simulating 200
virtual trials with the residual removed shows the same spread.

```{r btv, fig.cap = "Week-16 ACR20 for deucravacitinib 6 mg QD in a phase 2 PsA trial, 200 simulated trials (between-trial random effects only)."}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260505)
nTrials <- 200
armsBtv <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nTrials), function(i) {
  model1Arm(i, "DEUCRAVACITINIB", relDose = 1, times = 16)
}))
solBtv <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod1, "sigma"), armsBtv, returnType = "data.frame")
btvQ <- 100 * stats::quantile(solBtv$prob_acr20, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
knitr::kable(
  tibble(
    Quantity = c("2.5th percentile", "Median", "97.5th percentile"),
    `Simulated (% ACR20)` = round(unname(btvQ), 1),
    `Table S4 projection` = c(14.3, 51.4, 87.1)
  ),
  caption = "Between-trial spread of the deucravacitinib 6 mg QD week-16 ACR20 projection."
)

ggplot(solBtv, aes(100 * prob_acr20)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 25, fill = "grey70", colour = "grey30") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(14.3, 51.4, 87.1), linetype = c(2, 1, 2), colour = "red") +
  labs(x = "ACR20 at week 16 (%)", y = "Simulated trials") +
  theme_bw()

# Gate on the centre only: the simulated extremes depend on the RNG stream.
stopifnot(abs(btvQ[[2]] - 51.4) < 6)
```

The paper's interval also carries parameter uncertainty, which the packaged
model does not, so the simulated interval is expected to be similar or a little
narrower.

# Model 2: cross-endpoint bridge

## Reproducing Table 1 (Model 2 rows)

The paper feeds Model 1's ACR20 projections into Model 2 for a mixed
population (50% prior-TNF-experienced). The chain below does the same with
the Table 1 ACR20 values.

```{r table1-model2}
acr20In <- cmp1 |>
  filter(output == "prob_acr20") |>
  transmute(Treatment, phase, time, acr20 = sim)
armsM2 <- acr20In |>
  mutate(
    id = row_number(),
    cls = ifelse(Treatment == "Placebo", NA_character_, "TRT_ANTITNF")
  )
runM2 <- function(arms, wk, ui) {
  sub <- filter(arms, time == wk)
  dat <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(sub)), function(i) {
    model2Arm(sub$id[i], sub$acr20[i], sub$cls[i],
      phase3 = as.integer(sub$phase[i] == 3), priorTnfPct = 50, wk = wk
    )
  }))
  rxode2::rxSolve(ui, dat, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    select(id, prob_acr50, prob_acr70) |>
    left_join(sub, by = "id")
}
solM2 <- bind_rows(runM2(armsM2, 16, typ2wk16), runM2(armsM2, 24, typ2wk24)) |>
  pivot_longer(c(prob_acr50, prob_acr70), names_to = "output", values_to = "p") |>
  mutate(sim = 100 * p)

pubM2 <- tribble(
  ~Treatment, ~phase, ~output, ~time, ~pub, ~lo, ~hi,
  "Placebo", 2, "prob_acr50", 16, 8.21, 6.2, 10.81,
  "Placebo", 2, "prob_acr50", 24, 10.05, 7.5, 13.3,
  "Placebo", 2, "prob_acr70", 16, 2.57, 1.91, 3.45,
  "Placebo", 2, "prob_acr70", 24, 3.86, 2.83, 5.23,
  "Placebo", 3, "prob_acr50", 16, 7.82, 5.82, 10.46,
  "Placebo", 3, "prob_acr50", 24, 9.77, 7.17, 13.12,
  "Placebo", 3, "prob_acr70", 16, 2.47, 1.81, 3.37,
  "Placebo", 3, "prob_acr70", 24, 3.77, 2.72, 5.18,
  "Anti-TNF class", 2, "prob_acr50", 16, 25.98, 18.67, 34.99,
  "Anti-TNF class", 2, "prob_acr50", 24, 32.83, 23.8, 43.14,
  "Anti-TNF class", 2, "prob_acr70", 16, 11.94, 8.13, 17.27,
  "Anti-TNF class", 2, "prob_acr70", 24, 16.77, 11.41, 23.82,
  "Anti-TNF class", 3, "prob_acr50", 16, 18.67, 13.86, 24.72,
  "Anti-TNF class", 3, "prob_acr50", 24, 23.59, 17.5, 30.85,
  "Anti-TNF class", 3, "prob_acr70", 16, 7.54, 5.4, 10.48,
  "Anti-TNF class", 3, "prob_acr70", 24, 10.87, 7.74, 14.99
)
cmpM2 <- inner_join(pubM2, solM2, by = c("Treatment", "phase", "output", "time")) |>
  mutate(diff = sim - pub)
stopifnot(nrow(cmpM2) == nrow(pubM2))

cmpM2 |>
  transmute(
    Treatment, Phase = phase, Output = output, Week = time,
    `ACR20 input (%)` = sprintf("%.2f", acr20),
    `Published [95% CI]` = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", pub, lo, hi),
    Simulated = sprintf("%.2f", sim), Difference = sprintf("%+.2f", diff)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Model 1 -> Model 2 chain against Javidi 2026 Table 1 (percent responders).")

stopifnot(
  # Every chained value lies inside the paper's own 95% interval.
  all(cmpM2$sim >= cmpM2$lo & cmpM2$sim <= cmpM2$hi),
  max(abs(cmpM2$diff)) < 3
)
```

The chained values sit inside every published interval but are up to
`r sprintf("%.1f", max(abs(cmpM2$diff)))` percentage points from the published
centre, where the Model 1 rows agree to within a few hundredths. The Model 2
rows of Table 1 are summaries of 50,000 joint draws of both models'
parameters, and Model 2 is nonlinear in two uncertain inputs (the ACR20 draw
and the slope), so the summary need not equal the typical-value chain; a
transcription error would instead move a row by a whole slope or intercept
step, far outside its interval.

## External validation: ACR50 and ACR70 in IM011-084 (Table S4)

```{r tableS4-model2}
s4in <- solS4 |> transmute(id, Arm, acr20 = 100 * prob_acr20)
datS4m2 <- bind_rows(
  model2Arm(1, s4in$acr20[1]),
  model2Arm(2, s4in$acr20[2], "TRT_TYK2_INHIBITOR"),
  model2Arm(3, s4in$acr20[3], "TRT_TYK2_INHIBITOR")
)
solS4m2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(typ2wk16, datS4m2, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  left_join(s4in, by = "id") |>
  transmute(Arm, ACR50 = 100 * prob_acr50, ACR70 = 100 * prob_acr70) |>
  pivot_longer(c(ACR50, ACR70), names_to = "Endpoint", values_to = "sim")
pubS4m2 <- tribble(
  ~Arm, ~Endpoint, ~observed, ~pub, ~lo, ~hi,
  "Placebo", "ACR50", 10.6, 8.1, 6.2, 10.7,
  "Placebo", "ACR70", 1.5, 2.6, 1.9, 3.4,
  "Deucravacitinib 6 mg QD", "ACR50", 24.3, 24.7, 18.2, 32.5,
  "Deucravacitinib 6 mg QD", "ACR70", 14.3, 11.6, 8.2, 16.2,
  "Deucravacitinib 12 mg QD", "ACR50", 32.8, 27.1, 19.7, 36.1,
  "Deucravacitinib 12 mg QD", "ACR70", 19.4, 13.5, 9.3, 19.1
)
cmpS4m2 <- inner_join(pubS4m2, solS4m2, by = c("Arm", "Endpoint")) |>
  mutate(diff = sim - pub)
cmpS4m2 |>
  transmute(
    Arm, Endpoint, `Observed (IM011-084)` = observed,
    `Published projection [95% PI]` = sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]", pub, lo, hi),
    Simulated = sprintf("%.1f", sim), Difference = sprintf("%+.1f", diff)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Model 1 -> Model 2 week-16 projections for IM011-084 against Javidi 2026 Table S4 (percent responders; prior-TNF percentage set to the 57% reference, as the trial's is not reported).")

stopifnot(all(cmpS4m2$sim >= cmpS4m2$lo & cmpS4m2$sim <= cmpS4m2$hi))
```

Placebo is reproduced exactly; the deucravacitinib ACR50 / ACR70 chain runs
`r sprintf("%.1f", min(cmpS4m2$diff[cmpS4m2$Arm != "Placebo"]))` to
`r sprintf("%.1f", max(cmpS4m2$diff[cmpS4m2$Arm != "Placebo"]))` points above
the published centre, inside every interval. As for Table 1, the published
values summarise joint parameter draws of both models; the trial's
prior-TNF-experienced percentage is also not reported, and the 57% reference
used here is an assumption.

## Figure 4: ACR50 and ACR70 against ACR20

```{r fig4, fig.cap = "Model 2 typical ACR50 and ACR70 against ACR20 by drug class (phase 3, 57% prior-TNF-experienced) at weeks 16 and 24. Compare with the predicted points of Javidi 2026 Figure 4."}
grid <- expand.grid(
  acr20 = seq(10, 80, by = 2), cls = c(NA, classCols), wk = c(16, 24),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  filter(!(wk == 24 & cls %in% "TRT_TYK2_INHIBITOR"))
solF4 <- bind_rows(lapply(c(16, 24), function(w) {
  g <- filter(grid, wk == w)
  dat <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(g)), function(i) {
    model2Arm(i, g$acr20[i], g$cls[i], phase3 = 1, wk = w)
  }))
  ui <- if (w == 16) typ2wk16 else typ2wk24
  rxode2::rxSolve(ui, dat, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    select(id, prob_acr50, prob_acr70) |>
    bind_cols(select(g, -wk)) |>
    mutate(wk = w)
})) |>
  mutate(Class = ifelse(is.na(cls), "placebo", tolower(sub("TRT_", "", cls)))) |>
  pivot_longer(c(prob_acr50, prob_acr70), names_to = "output", values_to = "p")

ggplot(solF4, aes(acr20 / 100, p, colour = Class)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(output ~ paste("Week", wk)) +
  labs(x = "ACR20 (proportion)", y = "ACR50 or ACR70 (proportion)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

## Three files for two models

Model 2 is one model structure fitted twice, once to week-16 and once to
week-24 data, with different estimates (Table S3). Each fit is its own file;
neither is valid at other times.

## Model 1 outputs per indication

The source codes indication and endpoint as indicator columns of a single
response. The packaged model instead computes all three endpoint-indication
responses on every record (`prob_pasi75` for PsO, `prob_pasi75_psa` and
`prob_acr20` for PsA) with the same parameters and random effects, so one
solve gives a drug's PsO and PsA projections side by side. A user reads the
output that matches the trial; nothing in the fitted model changes.

## Unprinted dose normalisation

The paper normalises dose to 'the approved dose or the most frequent tested
dose for each compound' but does not list the regimens. The maintainers
recovered them from the paper's own typical-value curves and projections:
deucravacitinib 6 mg QD (Table S4, both doses reproduced within one
percentage point), and guselkumab 100 mg q8w, tofacitinib 5 mg BID and
secukinumab 300 mg (Figure S6 plateaus). Loading doses are ignored, as in
Figure S6, where the 10 mg/kg intravenous secukinumab loading arms follow the
150 mg curve.

## Unprinted prior-TNF normalisation

Model 2's prior-TNF covariate is 'the normalized observed values of %
population with prior-TNF experienced'; the normalisation is not given. The
packaged model uses `(PRIOR_TNF_PCT - 57) / 19`. The centre is the 'average of
% prior TNF-experienced = 57%' that the Figure S15 and S20 captions give as the
reference value. The scale was recovered by the maintainers from Figure S19,
whose prediction lines change by a known logit amount between 0% and 100%
prior-TNF: a joint fit of the 43 panels gives 18.5-19.7 percentage points per
normalised unit whatever the centre, while the centre itself is not
identifiable from that figure. The coefficient is 0.04-0.05 (SE 0.04), so
across 0-100% the covariate moves ACR50 or ACR70 by less than one percentage
point.

## Study-phase binning

The database holds phase 2a / 2b, 3b and 4 trials (Table S5), but both models
use a two-level phase 3 indicator. How the intermediate phases were binned is
not stated; `STUDY_PHASE3` should be 1 for phase 3 (and presumably 3b / 4) and
0 for phase 2 trials.

## Tofacitinib onset rate

The Model 1 onset-rate formula has no intercept and no tofacitinib term
(Data S1 code; Table S1 lists ten `k.drug` rows for eleven drugs), so
tofacitinib's log onset rate is 0 in PsO (rate 1 per week), shifted by the PsA
and ACR20 terms in PsA.

## Residual error

* Both models fix sigma to 1 and weight each record by the binomial variance
  of its arm proportion, which needs the arm size `N_ARM`. Each output's
  residual carries a `fixed(1)` multiplier and the weight is applied in
  `model()`. Typical-value simulations (`zeroRe()`) do not depend on it.
* Model 1 also has a continuous first-order autoregressive (`corCAR1`)
  correlation between the residuals of one arm over time. Its estimate is not
  reported, and rxode2 residuals are independent, so the packaged model omits
  it; it affects only the joint distribution of simulated observations, not
  any typical value.
* The Data S1 comment block labels `p.y` as 'logit transformation of observed
  ACR20 values' and `p.x` as 'observed values of ACR50 or ACR70', the reverse
  of Equation 5 and of the model formula `p.y ~ A*p.x + intc`. The packaged
  model follows Equation 5 (logit of ACR50 / ACR70 on the ACR20 proportion),
  which is the only reading that reproduces Table 1. The Model 2 residual
  weight `mdl.weights = 1/(p(1 - p)n)` is defined with p = observed ACR20 and
  is implemented that way.

## Scope

All three models simulate study-arm responder rates, not individual
patients. Model 1 random effects are between-trial; the paper's confidence
intervals additionally include parameter uncertainty, which is not part of the
packaged models.
